NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for
  viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday following the
  meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 852 4633 0491, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 852 4633 0491, Meeting Password: 066081
  Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
  following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand"
  option at the lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which
  item on the agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 12, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:02 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
Executive Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present: City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development and Public Works Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Planning Manager Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2020 "MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH
  AWARENESS MONTH"

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2020 "MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR SCHMITZ presented both proclamations, and spoke personally about the
importance of Maternal Mental Health and resources available.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN commended MAYOR SCHMITZ for speaking
passionately about this cause.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless
good cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  MAYOR SCHMITZ requested to remove item 5G from the Consent Calendar, to
  be added to New Business.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested amendments to items 5B and 5E.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A, 5C-D, and 5F,
  APPROVED AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 12, 2020
 C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – MARCH & APRIL 2020

  APPROVED WARRANTS 62753 THROUGH 62784 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $272,082.54 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040720 THROUGH
  040820; 050120; IN THE AMOUNT OF $104,390.55 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $376,473.09 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 4, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  2019 GENERAL PLAN ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORT

  DIRECTED STAFF TO TRANSMIT THE 2019 GENERAL PLAN APR TO
  THE GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF PLANNING AND RESEARCH (OPR)
  AND THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT (HCD), AS ATTACHED.

REMOVED FOR INDIVIDUAL CONSIDERATION

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF APRIL 28, 2020

  APPROVED.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF requested a correction on page 5 paragraph 3 of the
  draft City Council Minutes, to add “upon his announcement of his retirement” to
  her statement.

E.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 29, 2020

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted Debby Stegura was present for the GPAC
  Meeting, requesting this correction be made to the draft minutes.

There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN expressed his frustration on behalf of the community with
the recent announcement made by Los Angeles County regarding the “Stay at Home
Orders” continuing through the summer, and the confusing messages going out to the cities
and communities. He requested a recurring agenda item be placed on the agenda to provide
updates on COVID-19 reopening plans for the City, County and State.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL seconded COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s request to
agendize the COVID-19 reopening updates.

Public comment received from Eileen Hupp of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Chamber of
Commerce regarding a “Comprehensive Blueprint for Businesses to Reopen” created by
the Chamber, and requested to share this with the Council at a future meeting.

Public comment received from Robert Medawar expressing frustration as a business owner
with the inconsistencies in the County’s orders relating to local businesses.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 731, AN ORDINANCE OF CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES ADOPTING A NEW CHAPTER 17.78
  OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO THE
  PERMITTING OF SPECIAL EVENTS AND REPEALING MUNICIPAL CODE
  CHAPTER 5.64 REGARDING TEMPORARY USE PERMITS

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 12, 2020
   Recommendation: That the City Council 1) open the Public Hearing; 2) receive any
  public testimony; 3) discuss Ordinance No. 731; 4) continue the Public Hearing to
  the next Regular City Council Meeting; and 5) introduce Ordinance No. 731 on first
  reading.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Assistant City Manager Davis explained that fees were being surveyed right now,
  and would be provided in the City’s updated Fees and Charges Resolution, in
  response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF. She further explained that the fees within
  this ordinance were intended for large gatherings of more than 100 people, and
  that small gatherings would be permitted for record keeping and the fees would be
  minimal.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN inquired about discretionary language not
  included in the ordinance, allowing for the waiving of fees for certain organizations
  as the Council desires. City Attorney Davis explained that would be possible
  through the fee process.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ called for public testimony. Public comment
  was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live Zoom
  Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media
  platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL noted a correction needed on page 2 of exhibit
  A, attachment B, where two 2H’s are listed.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL,

  TO CONTINUE THE PUBLIC HEARING TO THE MAY 26, 2020 REGULAR
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING, AND INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 731 ON
  FIRST READING.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  B. CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPTION ON SECOND READING OF
  ORDINANCE 729, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AMENDING AND RESTATING CHAPTER 17.56
  (ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS) OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES
  MUNICIPAL CODE

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) receive any public testimony; 2) discuss
  Ordinance No. 729; 3) close the Public Hearing; 4) find that Ordinance No. 729 is
  exempt from the provisions of CEQA, per Section 15282(h), which provides a
  statutory exemption from CEQA for ordinances adopted pursuant to Government
  Code section 65852.2; and 5) conduct the second reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 729.

  Planning Manager Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  City Attorney Davis responded to concerns stated in a letter received by
  Californians for Homeownership, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 12, 2020
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN confirmed that an Accessory Dwelling Unit
  (ADU) cannot be built in a front yard as indicated in item D1 on page 4.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ called for public testimony. Public comment was invited via email,
  via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed
  on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms. No public
  testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  FOUND THAT ORDINANCE NO. 729 IS EXEMPT FROM THE
  PROVISIONS OF CEQA, PER SECTION 15282(H), WHICH PROVIDES A
  STATUTORY EXEMPTION FROM CEQA FOR ORDINANCES ADOPTED
  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65852.2; AND
  CONDUCTED THE SECOND READING AND ADOPTED ORDINANCE NO.
  729.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ANNUAL AUDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the agreement subject to the City
  Attorney’s approval for the CPA firm of Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP to
  perform CAFR audit for the Fiscal Year 2019-20, prepare the Pepper Tree
  Foundation’s tax returns, and review the GANN appropriation limitation.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the
  agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL stated that Council has been satisfied with this firm
  over the last year.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN confirmed there would be no late penalties if the
  audit was completed late.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED THE AGREEMENT SUBJECT TO THE CITY ATTORNEY’S
  APPROVAL FOR THE CPA FIRM OF ROGERS, ANDERSON, MALODY &
  SCOTT, LLP TO PERFORM CAFR AUDIT FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2019-
  20, PREPARE THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION’S TAX RETURNS,
  AND REVIEW THE GANN APPROPRIATION LIMITATION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 12, 2020
 B.  FISCAL UPDATE REPORT FOR YEAR-ENDING JUNE 30, 2020

  Recommendation: Receive and File.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the
  agenda material).

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL clarified that the pension obligation bond interest
  rate was reduced from approximately 7.75% to 3.62%, and shortened from 20 years
  to 10 years, as confirmed by Administrative Services Director Whitehead.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead explained that the roof leaks have been
  an issue for the past few years, the number of leaks would no longer be cost effective
  to repair, and a full new roof on both City Hall buildings is needed, in response to
  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF. He estimated the total cost of the project to be
  approximately $100,000 and that the City will solicit bids for the roof replacement.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN suggested that a three-ply underlayment be
  considered when the roof is replaced for a significant increase in the longevity of the
  roof, and encouraged staff to consider lifecycle costs.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN inquired about building permits on page 19 (page
  4 of the staff report). Community Development and Public Works Director Wahba
  discussed trends and projections for building permits.

  City Manager Grammer added that at the Council’s direction, extraordinary revenues
  are used to fund one-time projects.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN inquired about occupancy permits at the Country
  Club. Planning Manager Naughton reported approximately 12 units are physically
  occupied, with approximately 35-40 having final approval.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN commented on the conservative sales tax
  estimate. Administrative Services Director Whitehead stated that Target is not
  included in this fiscal year.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN confirmed that the resurfacing project out for bid
  would be using various special funds including SB1 funds.

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF TO RECEIVE AND FILE THE FISCAL UPDATE REPORT.

  There being no objection, MAYOR SCHMITZ so ordered.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

REMOVED FROM CONSENT AGENDA FOR INDIVIDUAL DISCUSSION

5G.  BUDGET AMENDMENTS FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Budget Amendments for
  Fiscal Year 2019-2020.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the
  agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 12, 2020
   COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL inquired about the change in numbers of the Park
  Facility Fees.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead confirmed that the Community Services
  increase was due to the ban on chemical pesticides within Bennett Landscape’s
  contract, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED THE BUDGET AMENDMENTS FOR FISCAL YEAR 2019-
  2020.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  City Manager Grammer informed the Council that a fiscal update would be brought
  to Council on a quarterly basis for the time being.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 730 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 8.20 (INTEGRATED WASTE
  MANAGEMENT)

  Recommendation: That the City Council conduct the second reading and adopt
  Ordinance No. 730.

  Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

  Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and
  during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website
  and social media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  CONDUCTED THE SECOND READING AND ADOPTED ORDINANCE
  NO. 730.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

City Attorney Davis provided an update on an issue that is now resolved regarding a
construction site using a waste hauler other than the City’s exclusive waste provider Waste
Management.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL reported that the Southern California Association of
Governments (SCAG) met last week, and approved the regional transportation plan
Connect SoCal. She also reported that at this meeting, the Regional Council approved the
RHNA appeals procedures which are now posted on the SCAG RHNA webpage. She stated
that this was her last meeting on the Regional Council as she has stepped down.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported that the Rolling Hills Estates Neighborhood Council
met last week, and received updates from the Lomita Sheriff on crime statistics in the City.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MAY 12, 2020
 COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported that the Steering Committee of South Bay Cities
Council of Governments (SBCCOG) met yesterday. PV Transit has joined the commitment
with American Dark Fiber network.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN added to COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL’S SCAG
report, adding that a delay in approval of the Connect Socal plan was requested by several
major organizations including the Leadership Council, to make considerations of the “new
normal” we are facing due to the pandemic. His motion on the Community, Economic and
Human Development Committee (CEHD) then moved it forward to the Regional Council.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN reported that the Clean Power Alliance (CPA) was facing
new challenges with respect to bill payments and energy loads. Businesses are using less
energy and residents are using more during the Stay at Home Orders.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN commented that the LA County West Vector Control
meets quarterly, in response to MAYOR SCHMITZ’S comment on recent mosquitos.
MAYOR SCHMITZ reminded the community to please empty any still water in plants, pots
and yards to reduce mosquitos.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL commented on her trip to China last summer with
Senator Ben Allen to forge friendships with local officials in China, carried out by the
Chinese People’s Friendship Association. The Association reached out recently and has
delivered a box of masks to the City. Staff will be looking to local first responders in need
of these donated masks.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL also reported that the Equestrian Committee met on
Monday, and recommended holding the annual Mayor’s Breakfast Ride on July 4 this
year.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF thanked Staff for completing the Senior Resources Guide,
and reminded residents that this resource is available now on the City’s website. She also
reported that the Regional Resource Guide from the SBCCOG will be out soon as well
with resources for the Community.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported that School Board Member Linda Reid has a Volunteer and
Senior Connection list, and is connecting volunteers with seniors in need of assistance.
Contact information can be found on the City’s website.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN reported that this week would have been the California
Contract Cities Associations Municipal Seminar, which was canceled due to the
pandemic. CCCA will be holding a virtual swearing-in this Saturday, May 16 at 6:00 p.m.
to swear in the incoming President and Secretary Treasurer. He also reported that in lieu
of the CCCA Municipal Seminar, CCCA will be doing a series of virtual talks beginning
this Thursday in sponsored by USC and CCCA, discussing relevant topics to local
governments. There will be four talks, one talk a week during the lunch hour.

MAYOR SCHMITZ reported on her weekly calls with the 88 Mayors of Los Angeles
County, and her twice-monthly calls with the Peninsula Cities Mayors. Local beach city
Mayors on these calls have requested to not allow beaches to open on Friday or Saturday
to prevent overcrowding on weekends after being closed for so long. She also reported
on the weekly calls with L.A. County Public Health Director Dr. Ferrer, expressing her
frustration in the confusing messaging that has been coming out recently.

City Manager Grammer reported that Rolling Hills Estates is still operating under the
County’s Safer at Home order, including the most recently revised order released late last
week allowing for the reopening of golf courses and hiking trails. On Saturday the City’s
hiking trails were reopened, with signage indicating physical distancing and face-covering
requirements. The revised order also allowed the reopening of specific retail stores – toy
stores, book stores, music stores, clothing stores, sporting good stores and florists – for
curbside pickup only. A reopening plan for City Hall has been developed. City Hall will be
